notes: Cases mirror the 'CASES' style used by run_test_NIST_buffer_standards_with_recipe.py: name, recipe_mol_L, acid_pKas, pH_ref, tol, etc.
If pH_ref is omitted, the runner will compute and report pH but will not PASS/FAIL.
Pressure-based CO2-saturated-water/brine benchmarks use literature values measured under pure-CO2 headspace at the stated total pressure (i.e., pCO2 ~= P_total).
Some hydrate names use the Unicode middle dot '·' to match CHEM_DB keys (e.g., MgSO4·7H2O). If your CHEM_DB uses ASCII '.', adjust accordingly.

CASES.name: High-purity water equilibrated with ambient air (CO2 ~ 400 ppm) at 25C

references.citation: Thornton / SnowPure application note on high-purity water pH (air-equilibrated water ~ pH 5.6 at 25C).
references.notes: Common reference for the widely-cited pH of air-equilibrated pure water.

CASES.name: THERMO: CO2-saturated pure water at 20C under pure CO2, P = 0.23 MPa (~2.27 atm)

references.citation: Haghi et al. (Tohidi group) – 'pH of CO2 saturated water and CO2 saturated brines' reports pH for CO2–H2O at multiple pressures/temperatures; Table 3 includes 293.15 K, 0.23 MPa: pH ~ 3.78.
references.notes: Strong thermodynamic benchmark (measured pH under pure CO2 headspace).

CASES.name: THERMO: CO2-saturated pure water at 50C under pure CO2, P = 0.23 MPa (~2.27 atm)

references.citation: Haghi et al. – CO2–H2O electrometric measurements; Table 3 includes 353.15 K, 0.23 MPa: pH ~ 4.00.
references.notes: Thermodynamic benchmark demonstrating temperature dependence under fixed CO2 pressure.

CASES.name: THERMO/APPLIED: CO2-saturated brine at 25C, NaCl ~1.03 m, pure CO2 at ~1 atm -> pH ~3.76

references.citation: Crolet & Bonis (1983) as summarized/cited in Haghi et al. – at 298.15 K and ~0.1 MPa, reported pH decreases with ionic strength; around ionic strength ~1.03 m: pH ~ 3.76.
references.notes: Useful brine benchmark; note your model may not include full Pitzer activity corrections (expect larger deviation).

CASES.name: THERMO/APPLIED: CO2-saturated brine at 25C, NaCl ~3.87 m, pure CO2 at ~1 atm -> pH ~3.57

references.citation: Crolet & Bonis (1983) as summarized/cited in Haghi et al. – at 298.15 K and ~0.1 MPa, pH decreases from ~3.76 to ~3.57 as ionic strength increases from ~1.03 m to ~3.87 m.
references.notes: High-salinity stress-test; deviations may reflect missing activity corrections rather than carbonate chemistry errors.

CASES.name: Cell-culture bicarbonate equilibrium: ~22 mM NaHCO3 + 5% CO2 at 37C -> pH ~7.4

references.citation: Michl et al., 2019 (Communications Biology) – discusses preparing media with 22 mM NaHCO3 and equilibrating in 5% CO2 to reach target pH ~7.4.
references.notes: Used here as a practical 'cell-culture analogue' equilibrium check.

CASES.name: DMEM-style guidance case: 5% CO2 at 37C commonly yields pH ~7.5–7.6 (convention/guidance)

references.citation: CultureCollections guidance note – states that using 5% CO2 with DMEM commonly results in pH ~7.5–7.6.
references.notes: This is a 'guidance benchmark' rather than a strict thermodynamic standard; good for sanity checking.

CASES.name: Industrial/biorelevant bicarbonate benchmark: mHanks buffer maintained at pH 6.8 ±0.05 by continuous CO2 sparging (37C)

references.citation: Liu et al., 2011 – describes mHanks bicarbonate buffer and that pH was maintained at 6.8 ±0.05 by continuously sparging CO2 at 37°C; composition given in Methods.
references.notes: A strong benchmark because the pH target and maintenance method are explicit and the ionic recipe is published.

CASES.name: Phosphate buffer + 5% CO2 'biotrap' case (REPORT-ONLY): 50 mM phosphate at pH 7.4, exposed to 5% CO2 (37C)

references.citation: Michl et al., 2019 – discusses how non-volatile buffers acidify upon exposure to 5% CO2 (general mechanism); phosphate is a non-volatile buffer system.
references.notes: No single canonical equilibrium pH is universally cited for this exact phosphate/CO2 system; use this case as a qualitative check unless you supply your own measured pH_ref.

CASES.name: NH3 + CO2 (applied): 0.5 M aqueous NH3 exposed to CO2; pH levels off to ~8.5 near CO2 saturation (20C)
notes: This is an applied benchmark: Atzori et al. report a dynamic absorption experiment where pH stabilizes near ~8.5 at CO2 saturation for ~0.5 M NH3 at ~20C.

To make this fully quantitative in your framework, add/enable an explicit NH3/NH4 total system in your chemistry core (if not already present) and represent initial NH3 via an appropriate CHEM_DB entry (e.g., 'NH3(aq)' or equivalent) rather than NH4Cl.

references.citation: Atzori et al., 2023 (Chemical Engineering Journal) – reports that during CO2 absorption into 0.5 M NH3 at ~20°C, pH drops and then levels off to about 8.5 as CO2 saturation is approached.
references.notes: Included as an applied NH3–CO2 benchmark; not a strict equilibrium standard, but useful for sanity checking NH3–carbonate coupling when your NHx chemistry is enabled.
